entries.definition: bewildering or striking dumb with wonder
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The heaviest impact here, and it lands on the person rather than rating the claim - covering both being thrown into confusion and being silenced by wonder.

entries.definition: barely credible
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Leaves the thing just this side of belief where *incredible* puts it past, and the strain it puts on belief sounds like extravagance rather than a fault.
examples: the fabulous endurance of a marathon runner

entries.definition: too improbable to admit of belief
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flat measuring word of the set - it sets the odds against the thing and leaves the mockery and the wonder to its neighbours.

entries.definition: beyond belief or understanding
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts the thing wholly outside belief or understanding rather than at the far end of the odds, and says nothing about whether what exceeds them is splendid or appalling.
examples: at incredible speed
the book's plot is simply incredible

entries.definition: too improbable to admit of belief
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Refuses belief with wonder still in it: the thing is too wonderful to be admitted, not too flimsy, unlike *tall*.

entries.definition: too improbable to admit of belief
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Dismissive without heat - the claim is treated as stretched in the telling, where *improbable* only weighs the odds.
examples: a tall story
He came home with a tall story about wolves in the lane.

entries.definition: be characteristic of
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flatly descriptive — the trait simply belongs to the thing, and no verdict on its worth comes with it.

entries.definition: be a distinctive feature, attribute, or trait; sometimes in a very positive sense
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The dry one: the trait is what separates this thing from that one, with none of the credit *distinguish* carries.

entries.definition: be a distinctive feature, attribute, or trait; sometimes in a very positive sense
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The member that leans hardest on the very positive reading the sense allows — the trait does not merely identify the thing, it raises it above what stands beside it.

entries.definition: be a distinctive feature, attribute, or trait; sometimes in a very positive sense
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Registers the trait as a sign the thing carries, crediting it lightly where *distinguish* lifts it.
examples: there is that in her features which marks the young woman of distinguished birth
every sentence of her uncle, which marked his intelligence, his taste, or his good manners

entries.definition: accept as true; take to be true
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The unmarked word for taking something to be true, carrying no judgement on whether the acceptance was earned.
examples: We didn't believe his stories from the War
She would not believe the story until she saw the letter herself.

entries.definition: accept as true
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Blunt and informal where *believe* is plain, it treats accepting a claim as taking something on offer, so the acceptance sounds weighed rather than simply held.
examples: I can't buy this story
He says the delay was the weather's fault, but I don't buy that.

entries.definition: believe to be the case
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal, and it frames the belief as arrived at rather than merely held, giving it a footing *believe* does not claim.

entries.definition: believe or accept without questioning or challenge
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Disparaging of the believer rather than the claim, since the gloss builds the absence of questioning into the acceptance itself.
examples: Am I supposed to swallow that story?

entries.definition: believe to be the case
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Softer than *believe*: it presents the belief as settled information one has come by, which lets the speaker hold it lightly.
examples: I understand you have no previous experience?
I understood that there were some very strong objections against the lady.

entries.definition: regard as untrustworthy; regard with suspicion; have no faith or confidence in
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Flat and settled — the plain negative of trusting, delivered as a standing verdict rather than as the charge carried by *suspect*.

entries.definition: regard as untrustworthy; regard with suspicion; have no faith or confidence in
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The wariest of the three, sounding like a misgiving felt about someone rather than a conclusion reached about them.

entries.definition: regard as untrustworthy; regard with suspicion; have no faith or confidence in
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The most accusing of these: it does not just withhold faith but pins something on its object, where *distrust* only declines to trust.
examples: I suspect her true motives
She suspected his motives from the first and would not take his help.

entries.definition: morally objectionable behavior
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flat, absolute name for conduct that offends morality, condemning without argument or degree.
examples: there is, I believe, in every disposition a tendency to some particular evil, a natural defect

entries.definition: a disrespectful act
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The lightest blame here: an act that withholds due respect rather than one that breaks anything.

entries.definition: a disrespectful act
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Frames the disrespect as a breach, something owed and transgressed, giving the act a hard formal weight that *irreverence* lacks.

entries.definition: morally objectionable behavior
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Condemns the same conduct with a moralizing relish, as though the wrong were knowingly savoured rather than merely done — fuller-blooded than the bare *evil*.

entries.definition: a deliberate pretense or exaggerated display
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Convicts the pretence of being both calculated and laid on too thick, so the fault is excess as much as falsity.

entries.definition: pretending that something is the case in order to make a good impression
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The mildest word here for faking it, faulting the wish to look good rather than the falsehood itself, which is where *pretence* puts the blame.
examples: he is wise enough to assume even the appearance of what is right

entries.definition: the act of giving a false appearance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flat, general name for putting up a false front, with none of the flattering motive that softens *appearance* and no charge of overdoing it; British spelling.

entries.definition: pretending that something is the case in order to make a good impression
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Treats the same impression-making pretence as something staged for onlookers, with more of a sneer at the performance than *appearance* carries.
examples: that ceremony is just for show

entries.definition: belligerence aroused by a real or supposed wrong (personified as one of the deadly sins)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain name for the belligerence, and the gloss lets the provoking wrong be merely supposed as readily as real, so the blame lands lighter than in *wrath*.
examples: Anger is counted among the seven deadly sins.

entries.definition: reprehensible acquisitiveness; insatiable desire for wealth (personified as one of the deadly sins)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Condemns while it defines — acquisitiveness called reprehensible and a wanting of wealth that nothing can fill.
